result.summary: This unit is the build surface and C ABI wrapper of libvaxis, a Zig terminal UI library: build.zig, the pinned dependency manifest, the C header, and src/c_api.zig, which exports screen, window, parser, TTY, runtime and embedded-terminal functions. I checked the build script for build-time execution, downloads and code generation, and the C API for hidden network use, secret access, backdoors and load-time side effects. I found none: all behaviour matches a terminal UI library.

findings.title: Build script is conventional
findings.detail: build.zig defines library, example, bench, test and docs steps. It reads build.zig.zon with @embedFile only to get the version string. It runs no external commands, downloads nothing and generates no code beyond a version option. Run steps exist only for the example, bench and test targets.

findings.title: Dependencies pinned by commit and hash
findings.detail: The zigimg and uucode dependencies are fetched from GitHub at fixed commits and verified against Zig package hashes. Both are well-known libraries that fit the module's purpose.

findings.title: C API can spawn a caller-specified program in a PTY
findings.detail: vaxis_terminal_new/spawn start the program named in the caller's argv inside a PTY. This is the documented embedded-terminal widget, and the child is chosen by the host application, not by the library.

findings.title: F3 key during query used for capability detection
findings.detail: applyRuntimeEvent treats an F3 key with shift or alt during terminal querying as a capability reply for explicit width or scaled text. This mirrors upstream vaxis.Loop, which detects these features through cursor-position reports. It only toggles rendering capabilities and grants no access.

data_flows.what: Escape sequences for rendering, alt screen, mouse mode, bracketed paste, window title, terminal capability queries, and Kitty graphics image data or file paths, all supplied by the calling application.
The argv, environment entries and working directory given by the caller, plus key events the caller forwards to the embedded terminal.
data_flows.to: child process spawned in a PTY (vaxis_terminal_spawn)
